In the vulnerable versions, `sensitiveHeaders` arrays from another realm were ignored and custom credentials could follow redirects. Only the Node.js HTTP adapter is affected, and there are no API changes. (__#11410__)

changes.change: **Header Defaults:** Only plain objects, null-prototype maps, and compatible `AxiosHeaders` instances are treated as common or method-specific defaults; literal headers such as `Link` are now preserved. Applications using custom class instances as defaults must convert them to plain maps, for example `{ post: { ...customDefaults } }`, or compatible `AxiosHeaders`. Otherwise, those instances become literal header values, including on requests using other methods. (__[#11156](https://github.com/axios/axios/pull/11156)__)
